purpose: A bounded method for choosing where to stand in the residential solar sales channel - commissioned representative, dealer, or referral partner - and then running the acquisition side of that position honestly: reconstructing from the signed agreement how a commission and its clawback exposure are actually produced, assembling a lead-channel portfolio judged on cancellation-adjusted cost per installed deal rather than cost per lead, screening homeowners for ownership, consumption, site red flags and financing readiness at screening depth with a scripted willingness to disqualify, and sizing a forward pipeline against the long signature-to-permission-to-operate cycle so income planning uses expected rather than signed value.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the business sells residential retrofit solar to owner-occupiers and does not itself hold the contractor, electrical, or structural licence; the system is built and energized by a licensed installer partner

income is transactional - commission or fee per installed system - with no contracted recurring revenue stream, so the only durable compounding asset in this vertical is reputation and the referral flow it produces

the channel structure described (commissioned representative, dealer or sales organization, referral or affiliate partner) is the common shape of the residential market, but every licensing, consumer-protection, contact-consent, and referral-compensation rule named here is an obligation class whose current form must be verified with the issuing authority in each jurisdiction sold into

every rate, spread, fee, price, savings figure, production number, and conversion or cancellation rate is treated as a mechanism to be measured or read from a specific document, never as a value this knowledge base supplies
exclusions: proposal-depth site and usage work - consumption analysis against the utility rate schedule, roof orientation, tilt and shade modelling, production estimation, offset design, proposal integrity and rate-escalator honesty, the disclosure-first explanation of cash, loan, lease and power-purchase-agreement structures, and permitting and interconnection process literacy - all of which belong to the sibling site-qualification, proposal-integrity and financing-literacy knowledge base

installer partner selection on build quality and install backlog, post-signature handoff and install-timeline communication with the homeowner, the operational administration of cancellations and clawbacks with the installer, the referral engine built from verified-happy installs, and reputation management as this vertical's durable asset, all of which belong to the sibling installer-partnerships, pipeline and reputation knowledge base

stating any specific commission rate, per-watt spread, dealer fee, lead price, savings amount, production figure, conversion rate, cancellation percentage, cooling-off period length, or market size as fact; every such number is described here only as a mechanism - where it comes from, what moves it, and which document or measurement establishes it for a given deal

contractor, electrical, and structural licensing, bonding, workmanship warranty obligations, engineering and code compliance, all of which belong to the licensed installer and are never assumed or promised by the selling side

personalized financial, tax, legal, or insurance advice to a homeowner, including whether a tax credit or incentive applies to a particular household, whether a household should finance, and which financing structure is best for them; those are the homeowner's decisions with their lender and their own advisors
system design, equipment selection, sizing, and production estimation, which are engineering work performed by the installer and modelled in the sibling proposal knowledge base

high-pressure and misleading-savings technique of any kind - manufactured scarcity, same-visit-only pricing, guaranteed savings or bill-elimination claims, implying affiliation with a utility or a government programme, or obscuring who the homeowner is contracting with - which is excluded as prohibited conduct rather than merely discouraged practice

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ETHICAL_SELLING_IDENTITY states the standing conduct rules in checkable form (every figure traceable to a homeowner-verifiable source, no guarantee, disclosed principal, no manufactured deadline) and HONEST_DISQUALIFICATION_PRACTICE supplies the scripted walk-away that proves the rules are real

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MARKET_MODEL_SELECTION distinguishes the three positions by who owns the lead record, who funds acquisition, who carries cancellation cost, and which obligation classes attach

competency_questions.question: Which licences, registrations, and permits attach to me as the seller rather than to the installer, and how do I confirm them for each town and state I sell into?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LICENSING_AND_REGISTRATION_CLASSES enumerates the seller-side obligation classes, names the verify-with-the-issuing-authority-per-jurisdiction rule, and holds the contractor-licensing boundary at the installer

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VULNERABLE_HOMEOWNER_CARE lists the recognition signals and the procedural response - slow down, involve a trusted person, provide language-appropriate documents, decline a same-visit signature, disqualify when the commitment plainly does not fit

competency_questions.question: How many leads and held appointments must exist now to produce installed, fully-paid deals three months out, and how do I plan personal cash flow across that gap without letting money pressure change how I sell?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SALES_CYCLE_STAGE_MODEL defines the countable stages through permission to operate, PIPELINE_MATH_AND_BUILD_AHEAD works backwards through stage survival ratios and lags to required current input, and INCOME_TIMING_AND_RESERVE_PLANNING sets the rule that money inside a clawback window is not yet spendable

glossary.definition: The floor price per watt or per system that the installer or dealer requires for a project; the seller's pay under a spread mechanism is a function of how far above this floor the homeowner is priced, which is exactly why the redline structure and the anti-pressure identity have to be reconciled deliberately rather than left implicit.

A compensation mechanism in which the commission equals the difference between the contracted price per watt and the redline, multiplied by system size; pay therefore scales with both how large the system is and how high the homeowner's price is, and the actual multiplier lives in the signed compensation agreement rather than in any recruiting claim.

The contractual recovery of commission already advanced to the seller when the underlying project fails to reach the milestone the advance was conditioned on - cancellation, failed financing, failed survey, refused interconnection, or expiry - typically recovered by netting against future commissions and, in some agreements, pursued as a debt when no future commissions exist.

The staged release of commission against project events rather than at signature - commonly a portion at contract or completed design, a portion at installation, and the remainder at permission to operate - with a holdback or reserve retained against later cancellations; the exact stages, proportions, and release conditions are set by the specific agreement.

The utility's authorization for the finished, inspected system to be energized and interconnected; it is usually the last event in the project timeline and frequently the trigger for the final commission portion, which is why a seller's income clock is set by a utility process the seller does not control.

The period after a home-solicitation sale during which the homeowner may cancel without penalty, together with the requirement that a written notice of that right be given in a prescribed form; both the length of the window and the notice requirements are jurisdiction-specific obligation classes to be verified with the applicable authority, never assumed.

A purchased lead sold simultaneously to several sellers versus one sold to a single buyer; sharing changes the economics through contact races, homeowner irritation, and lower close rates, so exclusivity, delivery order, and the number of co-buyers are contract terms to establish before spending rather than after.

A lead delivered or resold some time after the homeowner's original enquiry; age degrades contact rate and intent independently of the seller's skill, which is why lead age at delivery is a diligence question and why a contact-rate collapse should be investigated at the vendor before it is blamed on a representative.

A sit is an appointment the homeowner actually keeps with the decision-makers present; the sit rate is held appointments divided by appointments set, and it is the diagnostic that separates a lead-source problem from a setting-conversation problem, since set-but-not-held appointments consume the seller's most expensive resource without producing anything.

Total spend on a channel divided by the deals from that channel that reached installation and final payment, rather than by leads or by signatures; it is the only channel-comparable cost figure in this business because it absorbs contact rate, sit rate, close rate and post-signature attrition into one number the operator measures from their own records.

nodes.definition: Establish, before any channel, compensation, or hiring decision is made, that this business sells by verified numbers at the homeowner's pace, because residential solar's selling reputation has already been damaged by high-pressure closing and invented savings claims and every new seller inherits that suspicion at the door. The identity is a set of standing rules the operator commits to in advance rather than judges case by case: every figure shown to a homeowner traces to a source the homeowner can independently check - their own utility bill and usage history, the published rate schedule, the installer's site-specific production model, the lender's own disclosure document; no savings, payment, production, or bill-elimination figure is ever stated as guaranteed; there is no same-visit-only price, no manufactured deadline, and no signature taken at a visit the homeowner did not expect; the homeowner is told plainly who the seller works for and which licensed company will actually build the system; and the seller says out loud that a household is not a good fit when the screens say so. This node is the dominance root of the knowledge base: where it collides with a quota, a lead-spend recovery, or a personal cash-flow gap anywhere downstream, it wins, and the collision is resolved by changing the pipeline, not the conduct.

included: standing conduct rules covering sourcing, appointment, presentation and close
the traceable-number rule and the no-guarantee rule
disclosure of principal and of who builds the system
the obligation to state a non-fit plainly
extension of the same rules to subcontracted canvassers and junior representatives
excluded: the construction of the proposal itself and the production and savings modelling behind it, which belong to the sibling proposal-integrity knowledge base
installer selection and post-install reputation work, which belong to the sibling installer-partnership knowledge base
any assertion about what a specific savings or production figure will be

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a substantiated complaint, public review, or regulator enquiry alleging pressure or misleading savings against this seller or a canvasser working under its name

pros.claim: A rule decided in advance survives the moment of pressure, where a case-by-case judgement reliably does not
pros.example: a representative who has already committed to never taking a signature at an unscheduled first knock does not have to re-argue it at the end of a thin month

pros.claim: Traceable numbers turn the channel's bad reputation into a difference the homeowner can verify in the room within minutes
pros.example: opening the homeowner's own twelve-month usage history in their utility portal and building the conversation from it instead of from a quoted average-home figure

cons.claim: Anti-pressure selling loses deals a hard close would have caught, and on commission-only income that loss lands entirely on the operator this month
cons.example: a homeowner who says they want to think about it and never returns, where a same-night expiring discount would have produced a signature

cons.claim: The rules cannot be enforced by intention alone once other people sell under the operator's name, so they cost recruiting, training, and dismissal rather than a paragraph in a script
cons.example: a subcontracted canvasser using a scarcity line the operator never taught and the homeowner attributing it to the company

failure_modes: layering anti-pressure language over a process that is still built to close in one visit
holding the rules for the owner while tolerating breaches by subcontracted canvassers or newer representatives
letting a month-end shortfall silently suspend the rules and calling it an exception
treating the identity as marketing copy that never appears in a checkable behaviour
acceptance_tests: every figure in a live homeowner-facing document can be traced by the seller on demand to a source the homeowner can independently check
no live sales material or script contains a time-limited price, a guarantee of savings, or an implication of utility or government affiliation
the operator can name recent deals that were disqualified or declined on the screens rather than pushed forward
revisit_triggers: a complaint, review, or regulator enquiry alleging pressure or misleading savings against the seller or anyone canvassing under it
a new representative or subcontracted canvassing crew begins working under the operator's name
a compensation or quota change that increases pressure at a period boundary

nodes.definition: Decide which of the three structurally different positions in the residential solar channel this business occupies, because lead ownership, acquisition funding, cancellation exposure, licensing class, and the length of the wait for money all follow from that one choice. The commissioned sales representative sells another party's pricing under that party's agreement, is paid from a schedule the other party controls, usually carries clawback exposure on advances taken against their own future commissions, and risks little capital but also owns neither the customer records nor the pricing. The dealer or sales organization contracts with one or more installers, prices above a redline it negotiates, funds its own lead generation and its own representatives, and absorbs both the marketing cost and the cancellation cost of everything it signs - the most control and the most exposure. The referral or affiliate position never runs the sale at all: it introduces a screened homeowner to a licensed installer or dealer and is paid a defined fee at a defined milestone, earning the least per deal, controlling the least of the homeowner's experience, and carrying the fewest obligations - though referral compensation is itself a regulated class in many places and cannot be treated as a private arrangement. Choosing a position is choosing a risk and cash-flow profile, and hybrid positions must be named honestly to the homeowner rather than left ambiguous.

included: the three position classes and their control, capital and risk profiles
how the position determines lead-record ownership, cancellation-cost bearing and registration class
the honest naming of hybrid positions to the homeowner
excluded: which installer to partner with and on what build-quality or backlog criteria, which belongs to the sibling installer-partnership knowledge base
any assertion of specific commission rates, spreads, or referral fee amounts
the internal economics of the installer's own business

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in the installer or dealer agreement, in the operator's capital position, or in the registration classes a jurisdiction applies to the chosen position

pros.claim: A position chosen deliberately makes every downstream decision coherent instead of accidental
pros.example: an operator with a strong local network and no working capital choosing the referral position so no money is tied up in lead spend that pays out after a months-long project cycle

pros.claim: Naming the position exposes where cancellation cost actually lands before a cancellation discovers it for you
pros.example: a representative learning from the agreement, rather than from a first cancelled project, that an advance already spent is recoverable against future commissions

cons.claim: The choice is expensive to reverse because representatives, lead contracts, and installer agreements are all built around it
cons.example: a representative who has built a personal following under one dealer discovering that the customer records and lead history belong to the dealer, not to them

cons.claim: Hybrid positions blur accountability to the homeowner about who they are actually buying from and who stands behind the promise
cons.example: a paid introducer behaving like a salesperson, leaving the homeowner unsure whether their contract, their warranty, and their complaint route sit with the introducer or the installer

failure_modes: choosing on the headline compensation figure rather than on risk, capital need and cash-flow shape
operating as a de-facto dealer while registered and insured as nothing in particular
assuming the referral position carries no regulatory obligation because no contract is signed by the introducer
leaving the position undeclared so the homeowner cannot tell who they are dealing with
acceptance_tests: the operator can state for their position who owns the lead record, who funds acquisition, who bears cancellation cost, and which obligation classes attach
the position is reflected in a signed agreement rather than only in conversation, and the homeowner-facing introduction states it plainly
revisit_triggers: an installer or dealer materially changes its agreement, pricing, or redline terms
the operator begins paying for leads or engaging other people to sell
a jurisdiction adds or changes a registration class covering the current position

nodes.definition: Map the obligation classes that attach to the selling side specifically, and keep them cleanly separated from the contractor, electrical, and structural licensing that belongs to whoever actually builds and energizes the system. Depending on jurisdiction, a person selling home-improvement or solar contracts to homeowners may need a home-improvement or contractor's-salesperson registration tied to a specific licensed contractor, a solicitor's or peddler's permit for door canvassing issued per municipality and sometimes per person, a general business registration, and - where credit or financing is arranged or marketed - a separate credit-related registration class; entities marketing on behalf of a lender or a lease or power-purchase provider may additionally fall inside that provider's own oversight and training obligations. The expert work is to enumerate every class that could attach to the chosen position, confirm the current requirement with the issuing authority in each jurisdiction sold into rather than accepting an upline's assurance that everything is covered, hold dated documentary proof, and calendar every renewal with lead time. Thresholds, exemptions, reciprocity, and even which authority issues a permit differ by jurisdiction and change; verify current rules in your jurisdiction before relying on any of them.

included: enumeration of seller-side obligation classes for each position
per-jurisdiction verification with the issuing authority and dated proof
renewal calendaring with lead time
the boundary that build-side licensing is the installer's obligation
excluded: any statement of specific fees, thresholds, exemption tests, or licence numbers as fact
the installer's own licensing, bonding, and insurance file, which the sibling installer-partnership knowledge base verifies
legal advice on whether a particular activity requires a licence in a particular place

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a rule change, new ordinance, or authority notice in any jurisdiction sold into, or a change in the position or partner the registration is tied to

pros.claim: Verifying with the issuing authority rather than with a recruiter prevents building a pipeline that cannot lawfully be closed
pros.example: discovering before hiring a canvassing crew that a municipality requires a per-person solicitation permit with a background check and a lead time measured in weeks

pros.claim: A dated register with renewal lead time turns a business-ending administrative lapse into a calendar item
pros.example: a salesperson registration tied to one contractor needing to be re-filed when the operator adds a second installer partner

cons.claim: Per-jurisdiction verification is slow, must be repeated per territory, and quietly discourages expansion into adjacent towns where the pipeline is otherwise ready
cons.example: three neighbouring municipalities on one weekend canvass route with three different permit regimes and three different offices to visit

cons.claim: The register goes stale silently, because nothing in the day's work signals that a rule changed
cons.example: a municipality adding a do-not-knock ordinance mid-season with no notice to sellers already working the area

failure_modes: relying on an assurance that the dealer or installer covers the seller without ever seeing the document
letting a permit or registration lapse in the middle of an active campaign
assuming the referral position is exempt from every class without checking
treating one state's rules as the template for a neighbouring state
acceptance_tests: a current dated proof exists for every obligation class in every jurisdiction sold into, naming the issuing authority and the renewal date
the register distinguishes seller-side obligations from the installer's build-side licensing, and no seller-side document claims build-side authority
revisit_triggers: entering a new municipality or state, or adding a new installer partner the registration is tied to
a change in the sales position or in who sells under the operator's name
an approaching renewal date or a notice from an issuing authority

nodes.definition: Treat the at-the-door and in-home sale as its own regulated context rather than as an ordinary sales conversation that happens to occur in a house. Home-solicitation rules commonly impose a class of obligations that includes a written cancellation right with a stated cooling-off period, delivered in a prescribed form and sometimes in the language the sale was negotiated in; restrictions on canvassing hours; municipal do-not-knock registries and per-canvasser permit regimes; a duty to leave immediately when asked; prohibitions on misrepresenting the purpose of the visit, the identity of the company, or any affiliation with a utility, a government programme, or a neighbourhood initiative; and in a growing number of places, solar-specific disclosure documents that must accompany a residential agreement. The operational work is to know which class applies on each street worked, to build the cancellation notice into the signing packet as a normal part of it rather than an obstacle to be minimized, to honour a cancellation immediately and without friction or retention pressure, and to train and audit canvassers on the leave-when-asked rule. Requirements differ by jurisdiction and change frequently; verify current rules in your jurisdiction, and where two readings are possible, take the more protective one.

included: the home-solicitation obligation class and the written cancellation right as a mechanism
do-not-knock registries, permits, and hour restrictions
the prohibition on misrepresenting purpose, identity, or affiliation
canvasser training and audit on the leave-when-asked rule
excluded: stating the length of any cooling-off period or the content of any prescribed notice as fact, since both are jurisdiction-specific and changeable
the financing disclosure documents themselves and how their terms are explained, which belong to the sibling financing-literacy knowledge base
legal interpretation of whether a specific interaction constituted a home solicitation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an ordinance or statutory change in a worked jurisdiction, a complaint about door conduct, or a change in the required notice or signing packet

pros.claim: Presenting the cancellation right plainly at signing costs a few deals and removes the single most common basis for a later complaint or enforcement action
pros.example: the seller reading the cancellation notice aloud and dating it in front of the homeowner instead of leaving it in the back of a packet

pros.claim: Registry and permit compliance protects the neighbourhood relationship that referral flow in this vertical depends on
pros.example: a canvass route re-planned around a municipal do-not-knock list before the crew is dispatched rather than after a complaint

cons.claim: The rules genuinely reduce canvass productivity and vary street by street, which creates constant pressure to treat them as advisory
cons.example: a crew losing much of a Saturday route to permit boundaries and registry exclusions in a dense suburb

cons.claim: Compliance depends on the behaviour of the least-supervised person on the team, which the operator sees last
cons.example: a canvasser who keeps talking after being asked to leave, producing a complaint attributed to the company the homeowner never contracted with

failure_modes: treating the cancellation notice as a formality to be minimized or explained away at signing
working a street without the applicable permit because the crew was already there
implying a utility, government, or neighbourhood-programme affiliation to get through the first thirty seconds
responding to a cancellation with retention pressure rather than processing it
acceptance_tests: every signed residential agreement packet contains the applicable written cancellation notice, dated, and the seller can show where the requirement was verified
canvass routes are checked against the applicable permit and do-not-knock position before dispatch, with the check recorded
a cancellation received inside the window is processed without a retention attempt and logged with its date
revisit_triggers: working a new municipality or an ordinance change in an existing one
any complaint alleging misrepresentation at the door or refusal to leave
a change in the signing packet, the agreement form, or the financing product sold

nodes.definition: Recognize when the homeowner in front of you belongs to a group that a long-term financial commitment can harm disproportionately, and respond by changing the process rather than softening the pitch. The recognition signals are practical and observable: advanced age paired with a financing term that will outlive plausible tenure in the home; visible confusion, memory difficulty, or an inability to state back in the homeowner's own words what they would be agreeing to; a household whose fluent language is not the language of the documents; income that is fixed or benefit-based, where any new monthly obligation displaces something essential; evident pressure from a relative or a third party present; and a homeowner who has already been sold once this week by another door. The duty is procedural and specific: slow the process deliberately, offer to return when a family member or trusted advisor can be present, provide documents in the homeowner's language where the provider supplies them and never use a child of the household as an improvised interpreter for financial terms, decline a same-visit signature regardless of what the homeowner offers, and disqualify outright when the commitment plainly does not fit the household. This is procedural care and consumer protection, not financial advice, and it is a first-class rule of this business rather than a courtesy extended when convenient.

included: recognition signals for vulnerability in a home-sale context
the procedural response: slow down, involve a trusted person, language-appropriate documents, no same-visit signature
the duty to disqualify when the commitment plainly does not fit the household
excluded: any assessment of capacity, health, or cognition beyond observable difficulty understanding the transaction
personalized advice about the household's finances, benefits, taxes, or estate
the explanation of specific financing structures, which belongs to the sibling financing-literacy knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a complaint or family objection on a signed deal, a regulator focus on vulnerable-consumer protection in home sales, or a change in the languages served by the market worked

pros.claim: A procedural response protects the homeowner and the seller simultaneously, because the deals most likely to become complaints are the ones this rule stops
pros.example: returning a week later with an adult child present, and either signing a commitment everyone understood or ending it cleanly

pros.claim: The teach-back check - asking the homeowner to explain the commitment in their own words - is a cheap, reliable signal that needs no judgement about the person
pros.example: a homeowner who cannot say who they would be paying each month, which ends the visit regardless of their enthusiasm

cons.claim: The rule most often costs a deal that the homeowner themselves was eager to sign, which makes it feel paternalistic in the moment
cons.example: declining a same-visit signature from an enthusiastic elderly homeowner who insists they have already decided

cons.claim: Recognition signals are imperfect and can misread language difference or unfamiliarity as vulnerability, slowing a sale that needed no protection
cons.example: treating a homeowner who prefers to consult family as impaired rather than simply deliberate

failure_modes: noticing the signals and continuing anyway because the homeowner consented
using a family child or a neighbour as an interpreter for financing terms
documenting the care as performed when the visit in fact ended in a same-day signature
treating the rule as applying only to obvious extremes and not to fixed-income or language cases
acceptance_tests: no signature is taken at the same visit where a vulnerability signal was observed, and the deferral is recorded with its reason
the homeowner can state back in their own words who they would pay, for how long, and what happens if they move, before anything is signed
documents were available in the homeowner's language or the sale did not proceed
revisit_triggers: a complaint, cancellation, or family objection arising from a signed deal
adding representatives or canvassers who will meet homeowners unsupervised
entering a community where the dominant household language differs from the document language

nodes.definition: Understand commission as the output of a formula written in a specific contract, not as a rate quoted in a recruiting conversation. The mechanism classes in common use are: a spread, where pay is the difference between the price the homeowner contracts at and a redline or base cost set per watt or per system, multiplied by size, so pay rises with both system size and how far above the floor the homeowner is priced; a percentage of contract value; a flat amount per closed and installed system; and a fixed fee per introduced homeowner who reaches a named milestone. Sitting on top of the mechanism are modifiers that decide the real number: adders for batteries, roof work, or electrical upgrades that may or may not carry margin; deductions for lender or provider fees attached to particular financing products; a split that differs between a self-generated lead and a company-supplied one; overrides paid upward through a hierarchy; and volume tiers that move the base itself. The literacy work is concrete - reconstruct from the signed compensation agreement the exact arithmetic that converts one signed project into one payment, then verify that reconstruction line by line against the first real commission statement, and treat any discrepancy as a question to resolve in writing before the second deal. Every figure used in planning comes from that agreement and that statement; none of it comes from a recruiting claim, and this knowledge base supplies none of it.

included: the mechanism classes and their modifiers as structures
reconstructing one deal's arithmetic from the signed agreement
reconciling the reconstruction against the first commission statement
naming the structural tension between spread-based pay and homeowner price
excluded: any specific rate, spread, adder, dealer-fee percentage, override, or dollar amount
the homeowner-facing explanation of financing structures and their costs, which belongs to the sibling financing-literacy knowledge base
negotiation tactics for improving a compensation agreement

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an amendment to the compensation agreement or redline, a new financing product with different fee treatment, or a statement that fails to reconcile

pros.claim: Reconstructing the arithmetic converts a vague expectation into a per-deal number the operator can plan lead spend against
pros.example: discovering that a lender fee on one financing product changes the net enough to alter which channels can be afforded

pros.claim: Line-by-line reconciliation of the first statement surfaces misunderstandings while there is still one deal at stake instead of twenty
pros.example: an adder assumed to carry margin turning out to be passed through at cost

cons.claim: A spread mechanism structurally pays more when the homeowner pays more, which puts the compensation design in direct tension with the verified-numbers identity and cannot be resolved by good intentions alone
cons.example: a representative who can raise their own pay materially by pricing a homeowner higher for an identical system

cons.claim: The arithmetic is only as stable as the agreement, and redlines and tiers can be revised by the other party with little notice
cons.example: a redline moving mid-quarter so deals modelled at one net arrive at another

failure_modes: planning a business on a recruiting headline rate that no agreement supports
ignoring modifiers such as lead-source splits and product-specific fees until the statement arrives
never reconciling a statement against the contract because the number was close enough
presenting the spread structure to a homeowner as though price were fixed by the installer
acceptance_tests: the operator can compute the expected payment for one specific signed project from the agreement alone, before any statement arrives
the first commission statement has been reconciled line by line to that computation and any discrepancy raised in writing
revisit_triggers: any amendment to the compensation agreement, redline, tier, or lead-source split
the introduction of a new financing product, adder, or partner with different fee treatment
a statement that does not reconcile to the reconstructed arithmetic

nodes.definition: Draw the timeline of when money actually moves toward the seller and under what conditions it can move back, because in this vertical a signature is the beginning of the payment process rather than the end of it. Compensation is typically staged against project events rather than paid at contract: a first portion at signing or at completed site survey and design, a further portion at installation, and a final portion at inspection or permission to operate, with a holdback or reserve retained against cancellations that have not yet happened. Every stage before the last is conditional, and the trigger list that reverses it is specific and knowable: cancellation inside the rescission window, financing that fails verification, a site survey that changes or kills the design, a permit or interconnection refusal, a project that simply ages out of the queue, and in many agreements a separation of the representative from the dealer before the final milestone. Recovery is normally by netting against future commissions, and some agreements make the balance a personal debt when future commissions do not exist. The expert work is to extract from the agreement the exact trigger list, the recovery method, the reserve mechanism and its release condition, and the treatment on separation, then to hold spending to money that has passed the last trigger. These terms are set by the specific agreement and vary widely; read yours rather than assuming a market norm.

included: the milestone structure as a mechanism and the conditions attached to each stage
the clawback trigger list, recovery method, reserve mechanism and release condition
the separation treatment and the personal-debt possibility
the rule that money inside a trigger window is not yet earned
excluded: any specific proportions, amounts, holdback percentages, or window lengths
the operational work of preventing, communicating through, and administering cancellations with the installer, which belongs to the sibling installer-partnership knowledge base
advice on whether to accept a particular agreement

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an amendment to milestone, reserve or separation terms, a first clawback event, or a change of installer or financing partner that redefines the milestones

pros.claim: An explicit trigger list turns clawback from an ambush into a known and plannable exposure
pros.example: knowing before the first sale that a failed interconnection reverses a portion already advanced, and reserving against it from the first deal

pros.claim: Mapping the timeline reveals the true cash-conversion cycle of the business, which is what actually determines survivable lead spend
pros.example: recognizing that a project signed today pays its final portion only after a utility process the seller does not control

cons.claim: The exposure is real and largely outside the seller's control, since permitting, install queues, and interconnection belong to other parties
cons.example: a homeowner cancelling during a long install backlog after the seller did everything correctly

cons.claim: Reserving against clawback lowers usable income exactly when a new operator has the least of it, which is when the temptation to spend advances is strongest
cons.example: an operator in month two treating an advance as income and having no way to cover a reversal in month four

failure_modes: treating an advance as earned income and spending it before the last trigger passes
never reading the separation clause and discovering the balance treatment on the way out
assuming a reserve is released automatically without knowing its release condition
planning lead spend against signature volume rather than against milestone-cleared payments
acceptance_tests: the operator can list every clawback trigger, the recovery method, the reserve release condition, and the separation treatment, citing the clause for each
advanced-but-clawbackable amounts are held separately from spendable funds and reconciled at each milestone
revisit_triggers: an agreement amendment touching milestones, reserve, or separation
a first clawback event, or a rise in the rate of reversals
a change of installer partner or financing provider that alters milestone definitions

nodes.definition: Before building any part of the business on paid introductions, establish which class the payment falls into and what that class triggers, because paid referral is regulated in ways that a handshake between neighbours is not. Three arrangements that feel similar are legally distinct: paying an existing customer or an unlicensed member of the public for introducing a homeowner; paying a licensed trade professional such as a roofer, electrician, or real-estate agent for a stream of introductions; and receiving a fee oneself as an unlicensed introducer to a licensed installer or dealer. Jurisdictions differ on whether the payer must be licensed, whether the recipient must be, whether compensation to unlicensed persons for procuring home-improvement contracts is capped or prohibited, and what must be disclosed - and consumer-protection principles generally require that a homeowner be told when the person recommending a company is being paid for the recommendation. Where the introducer is a licensed professional, their own professional conduct rules on referral fees and disclosure bind them independently of anything the seller agrees. The work is to name the arrangement precisely, verify the applicable class with the relevant authority in the jurisdiction, put the disclosure to the homeowner in writing, and document the trigger and timing of the payment in an agreement rather than in a conversation. Verify current rules in your jurisdiction before offering or accepting any referral compensation.

included: the three arrangement classes and how they differ
per-jurisdiction verification of permissibility and disclosure duties
written homeowner disclosure and a documented payment trigger
the independent professional rules binding a licensed introducer
excluded: any statement of permitted fee amounts, caps, or specific rules as fact
the reputation-driven referral engine built from verified-happy installs, which belongs to the sibling installer-partnership and reputation knowledge base
legal advice on a particular referral arrangement

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a jurisdictional or professional-body rule change on referral compensation, or the addition of a new class of paid introducer

pros.claim: Naming the class first prevents building a channel that must later be dismantled and unwound with people the operator has to keep working with
pros.example: learning before launch that compensation to unlicensed persons for procuring home-improvement contracts is restricted in a target state

pros.claim: Written disclosure to the homeowner preserves the trust that makes a referral valuable in the first place
pros.example: telling a homeowner plainly that the neighbour who recommended the company receives a fee if they proceed

cons.claim: Disclosure reduces the persuasive force of a referral, which is precisely the asset being paid for
cons.example: a homeowner discounting a neighbour's recommendation once the fee is disclosed

cons.claim: Rules differ enough across neighbouring jurisdictions and professions that one uniform referral programme is often not possible
cons.example: a real-estate agent's own professional rules forbidding an arrangement that is otherwise permitted for an unlicensed neighbour

failure_modes: treating a referral fee as a private matter needing no disclosure
assuming a rule verified in one state applies in the next
paying a licensed professional without checking their own professional constraints
leaving the payment trigger undefined so the introducer and the seller disagree about a cancelled project
acceptance_tests: each referral arrangement in use is classified, verified against the jurisdiction with the source and date recorded, and documented in writing
every homeowner arriving through a paid introduction receives a written disclosure of the compensation before contracting
revisit_triggers: operating in a new jurisdiction or beginning to pay a new class of introducer
a professional body or authority updating referral-fee or disclosure rules
a dispute with an introducer about a payment on a cancelled project

nodes.definition: Plan the business around the gap between the day a homeowner signs and the day the last clawback trigger on that project expires, because that gap - not the headline commission - decides whether the operator survives long enough to build a pipeline that carries itself. The residential cycle runs from signature through financing verification, site survey, engineering, permitting, install scheduling, inspection, and utility interconnection, and any of those stages can stall for reasons the seller cannot influence, so a meaningful share of pay lands months after the work that earned it while lead spend, fuel, subscriptions, and household costs land immediately. Two structural consequences follow and both are planning rules rather than aspirations: an operator entering this business needs runway measured against the full cycle to final payment rather than against the first milestone, and money already received but still inside a clawback window is not the operator's money to spend. The mechanism is to hold advanced-but-reversible amounts separately, size a reserve against the operator's own measured cancellation and stall rates once enough deals exist to have any, front-load lead spend only to the level a bad quarter can absorb, and answer a thin month with pipeline volume built earlier rather than with a harder close now. This is operating-cash discipline for a commission-based business, not personal financial advice, and every figure in it is the operator's own measurement.

included: the signature-to-final-payment gap as the planning horizon
separating clawbackable receipts from spendable funds
sizing a reserve from the operator's own measured attrition
the rule that a thin month is answered with earlier pipeline, never with pressure
excluded: personalized financial, tax, or investment advice to the operator or anyone else
any specific reserve amount, runway length, or income figure
the homeowner's own financing decision, which belongs to the homeowner and their lender

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a measured change in the operator's cancellation rate, milestone timing, or committed fixed costs and lead spend

pros.claim: Planning against final payment rather than first milestone removes the most common reason new sellers leave the business in the first year
pros.example: an operator who funded a full cycle of living costs before starting, and therefore did not need a signature from a household that should have been disqualified

pros.claim: A reserve makes the anti-pressure rules affordable, which is what turns them from a stated value into an operating reality
pros.example: declining a same-visit signature in a slow month because the month does not have to be rescued by that one deal

cons.claim: Reserving reduces the capital available for lead generation exactly when growth would compound fastest
cons.example: holding back funds against reversals instead of buying the extra lead batch that would have filled next quarter

cons.claim: The reserve can only be sized honestly once the operator has enough of their own deals to measure attrition, so the first year runs on an estimate
cons.example: a new operator guessing at a cancellation rate and discovering the real one only after two quarters

failure_modes: treating milestone advances as income and building fixed costs on them
sizing runway to the first payment rather than to the final one
cutting lead spend in a thin month, which guarantees the next thin quarter
answering a cash-flow gap by relaxing the conduct rules for one deal
acceptance_tests: spendable funds and clawbackable advances are tracked as separate balances and reconciled at each milestone event
the reserve is sized from the operator's own measured cancellation and stall rates once available, with the measurement dated and re-run
revisit_triggers: a change in milestone or reserve terms in the compensation agreement
a measured rise in cancellation or a lengthening of install and interconnection timelines
a change in fixed costs, headcount, or committed lead spend

nodes.definition: Hold the channel menu as a portfolio with deliberately different cost, intent, and compliance shapes rather than chasing whichever channel is currently fashionable in the operator's peer group. Door canvassing spends labour and permits instead of media, produces the lowest-intent conversations in the menu, carries the heaviest consumer-protection load, and is the channel most responsible for the industry's damaged reputation - which makes it the channel where the conduct rules do the most work. Purchased leads convert media spend directly into contact attempts but arrive with consent provenance the operator did not create, variable intent, and, when shared, a race against other sellers. Self-generated digital presence - local search, community groups, a review-backed site, content that answers the questions homeowners actually ask - costs time and learning before it costs money and produces the highest-intent inbound of the paid classes, but it starts slowly. Introductions from past customers and trade partners convert best and cost least, yet cannot be scaled on demand and are only available once installs exist, which makes them a consequence of good delivery rather than a channel to be bought. Retail, event, and partner-supplied appointment channels sit in between with their own contractual strings. The work is to run a small deliberate mix, tag every lead with its channel and specific source, and let cancellation-adjusted cost per installed deal decide the mix rather than the price on the invoice.

included: the channel menu with its cost, intent and compliance shape
the portfolio principle of a small deliberate mix over a single channel
mandatory per-channel and per-source tagging
the rule that channel choice is decided on installed-deal cost
excluded: building the referral engine from verified-happy installs and the reputation work behind it, which belong to the sibling installer-partnership and reputation knowledge base
any specific lead price, cost per lead, or conversion figure
advertising creative and platform mechanics beyond their cost and compliance consequences

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a measured shift in a channel's installed-deal cost, or a vendor, platform, or ordinance change that alters its availability or compliance load

pros.claim: A mix protects the business against a single channel failing, which in this vertical happens abruptly through a vendor change, a platform policy, or a new local ordinance
pros.example: a canvass-only operator losing a season when a municipality adopts a do-not-knock ordinance mid-year

pros.claim: Per-source tagging is what later makes every economic comparison in this knowledge base possible at all
pros.example: discovering that one specific landing page, not the whole digital channel, produced every installed deal from that spend

cons.claim: Running several channels at once splits attention and volume so thinly that none of them reaches a sample size that can be judged
cons.example: four channels running simultaneously in a first quarter, none with enough installed deals to distinguish signal from variance

cons.claim: The cheapest and best-converting channel is the one that cannot be bought or accelerated, which tempts operators back toward volume channels for speed
cons.example: an operator with no installs yet having no referral flow available and therefore over-committing to purchased leads

failure_modes: adopting a channel because a peer reported success rather than because it fits the position and capital
leaving leads untagged so no channel can ever be evaluated
judging a channel on cost per lead and abandoning the one with the best installed-deal economics
scaling a channel before a cohort has been followed all the way to final payment
acceptance_tests: every lead record carries a channel and a specific source tag at creation, with no untagged intake path
each active channel has a defined trial size and a stated decision rule tied to installed-deal cost rather than to cost per lead
revisit_triggers: a channel's measured installed-deal cost moves outside its planned band
a vendor, platform policy, or local ordinance change that alters a channel's availability or compliance load
the first installs arrive and a referral channel becomes genuinely available

nodes.definition: Treat a lead vendor as a supplier whose contract terms decide in advance whether the spend can ever work, and verify before the first invoice rather than after the first bad month. The diligence set is specific: is the lead exclusive or shared, and if shared, with how many buyers and in what delivery order; what is the return or credit policy, what counts as a returnable lead - wrong number, renter, not the owner, outside territory, no recollection of enquiring - and inside what window must it be returned; how was consent to be contacted obtained, and can the vendor produce the artifact of it, meaning the form, the timestamp, the disclosure language, and the originating page, since responsibility for an unlawful contact generally follows the party who makes the call rather than the party who sold the list; how old is the lead at delivery and has it been sold before; was it co-registered from an unrelated offer so the homeowner never intended a solar conversation at all; and what volume commitment, minimum spend, or cancellation notice binds the buyer. The verification method is not a conversation but a small trial batch, tagged separately, worked by the operator's normal process, and judged on contact rate, sit rate, and eventually installed deals rather than on the vendor's own conversion claims. Never buy against a promised conversion rate, and never accept an assurance of compliance without the consent record behind it.

included: exclusivity, delivery order, return policy and window, lead age and resale history
consent provenance and the artifact that evidences it
volume commitment and exit terms
the separately tagged measured trial batch as the decision method
excluded: any specific lead price, promised conversion rate, or vendor name
the contact-consent obligation classes themselves, which are defined in the contact-compliance work unit
the appointment-setting script, which is diagnosed separately

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a measured drop in a vendor's contact or sit rate against its trial baseline, a consent complaint traced to its records, or a change in its terms

pros.claim: A return policy with a defined window converts a portion of unavoidable waste into recovered spend, and its absence is itself a signal about the vendor
pros.example: returning renter and wrong-number records inside the window instead of absorbing them as cost

pros.claim: Demanding the consent artifact filters out the vendors most likely to create legal exposure for the buyer, before any money is spent
pros.example: a vendor unable to produce the originating page and timestamp for a record, which ends the evaluation

cons.claim: A trial batch large enough to judge on installed deals takes a full project cycle to read, so the decision is made on early-stage proxies under uncertainty
cons.example: committing or walking away on contact and sit rates months before the first installed deal from that batch is known

cons.claim: Exclusive, consent-verified leads cost more per record, which looks unaffordable next to a shared alternative until installed-deal cost is computed
cons.example: an operator switching to a cheaper shared source and losing more in sit rate than the price difference saved

failure_modes: signing a volume commitment before a trial batch has been worked
accepting a compliance assurance without seeing a consent record
mixing trial leads into the general pool so the trial can never be evaluated
judging the vendor on the vendor's own reported conversion figures
acceptance_tests: the exclusivity, return policy and window, lead age, resale history, consent artifact, and exit terms are documented for each vendor before the first paid batch
each vendor's leads are tagged distinctly and a defined trial size and decision rule exist before spending scales
revisit_triggers: contact rate on a vendor's leads drops materially against its own trial baseline
a homeowner states they never requested contact, or a complaint arises from a purchased record
the vendor changes exclusivity, delivery, pricing, or return terms

nodes.definition: Know which obligation class governs each way this business reaches a homeowner, and build the records that prove the class was met for each specific homeowner. The classes commonly in play are: prior express written consent for automated or pre-recorded calls and for marketing text messages; national and state do-not-call registries with defined exemptions such as an existing business relationship or a homeowner's own recent enquiry; an internal do-not-call list that must honour an opt-out immediately, permanently, and across every representative and channel at once; calling-hour restrictions measured in the homeowner's local time; caller-identification requirements; one-party versus all-party consent for recording a call or a doorstep conversation; and email marketing rules requiring accurate identification and a working unsubscribe. Consent that arrived attached to a purchased lead is only as good as the artifact behind it, and the party making the contact normally carries the liability regardless of who sold the record. The operational work is unglamorous and unavoidable: store the consent artifact with the lead record at intake, scrub against registries before any campaign, propagate an opt-out everywhere within the business immediately, and retain the evidence for the period the applicable rules require. Requirements, exemptions, and enforcement intensity differ by jurisdiction and change; verify current rules in your jurisdiction and where readings conflict, take the more conservative one.

included: the consent, registry, internal-list, hours, identification, recording and email obligation classes
the per-lead consent artifact and its retention
immediate cross-channel opt-out propagation
the rule that liability follows the caller, not the list seller
excluded: any assertion of specific retention periods, penalty amounts, or exemption tests as fact
the door-solicitation and cancellation-right obligations, which are held in the home-solicitation work unit
legal advice on whether a specific contact was lawful

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a contact complaint or dispute, a new contact channel or tool, or a rule or enforcement change in a jurisdiction contacted

pros.claim: A consent artifact stored at intake is the only thing that answers a later challenge, and it costs nothing to capture at the moment the lead is created
pros.example: producing the timestamped enquiry form and its disclosure language when a homeowner disputes ever having asked to be contacted

pros.claim: One internal opt-out list applied across every channel and every representative prevents the repeat-contact pattern that generates most complaints
pros.example: a homeowner who opted out by text never being called again by a different representative working a different list

cons.claim: The record-keeping burden falls on the smallest operators hardest, since it has to exist from the first lead rather than from the first hire
cons.example: a solo operator maintaining registry scrubbing and consent storage before there is any volume to justify a system

cons.claim: Conservative readings of ambiguous rules cost reachable contacts that a more aggressive competitor will call
cons.example: declining to text a lead whose consent language does not clearly cover messaging

failure_modes: relying on a vendor's compliance assurance instead of holding the consent artifact
keeping an opt-out in one representative's phone rather than in the shared list
calling outside permitted hours because the lead's area code misled about local time
recording conversations without establishing the applicable consent rule
acceptance_tests: every lead record carries a retrievable consent artifact or an explicit basis for contact, and the retention period applied is documented
an opt-out test can be traced end to end: the request, the timestamp, and its propagation across every channel and representative
campaign lists show a dated registry scrub before dispatch
revisit_triggers: a complaint or dispute about contact, or a homeowner denying they enquired
adding a new contact channel, dialer, messaging tool, or recording practice
a rule change or enforcement development in a jurisdiction contacted

nodes.definition: Build the chain that converts money spent on a channel into money actually kept from that channel, measured entirely from the operator's own records rather than from industry claims or vendor promises. The chain is a sequence of ratios applied in order: spend divided by leads gives cost per lead; the share of leads reached gives contact rate; the share of contacts that become a held appointment gives sit rate, which is the expensive one because a set-but-not-held appointment consumes the seller's scarcest resource and produces nothing; the share of sits that produce a signed agreement gives close rate; and the step most operators omit entirely, the share of signed agreements that survive financing verification, survey, permitting, install, and interconnection to reach final payment. Dividing total channel spend by installed-and-paid deals gives cost per installed deal, the only figure comparable across channels, and comparing it against the net-per-deal produced by the compensation mechanism gives the channel's real contribution. The model must also carry time explicitly, because money leaves at the lead and returns across a months-long cycle, so a channel can be genuinely profitable and still insolvent at a given spend rate. Every ratio here is the operator's own measured value on a tagged cohort; borrowing someone else's numbers produces a precise model of a business that does not exist.

included: the ordered ratio chain from spend to installed and paid deals
cost per installed deal as the only cross-channel comparison
the timing dimension separating profitability from solvency
the requirement that every ratio be measured on the operator's own tagged cohorts
excluded: any supplied benchmark, industry average, or specific cost or conversion figure
the diagnosis of which stage broke when the chain degrades, which is a separate work unit
accounting, tax treatment, or financial reporting of the spend

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a cohort completing the cycle to final payment, a compensation change altering net per deal, or a stage ratio shifting beyond normal variation

pros.claim: Cost per installed deal makes structurally different channels comparable for the first time, which usually reverses at least one intuition the operator held
pros.example: an expensive exclusive source proving cheaper per installed deal than a shared source at a fraction of the price per record

pros.claim: Carrying time in the model exposes the solvency question that a pure margin calculation hides
pros.example: a channel with acceptable economics that cannot be run at the planned monthly spend because the payments arrive after the next three months of invoices

cons.claim: The full chain can only be closed after a cohort completes a long project cycle, so early decisions must still be made on partial evidence
cons.example: judging a channel at the sit-rate stage because no cohort has reached final payment yet

cons.claim: Small operators generate cohorts too small for the later ratios to be stable, so the model reports noise as though it were signal
cons.example: one cancelled deal in a small cohort moving cost per installed deal enough to condemn a viable channel

failure_modes: comparing channels on cost per lead because it is available immediately
omitting post-signature attrition and overstating every channel equally
mixing cohorts from different periods or vendors so no ratio is attributable
importing a benchmark conversion rate to fill a gap the operator has not measured
acceptance_tests: each active channel has a computed cost per installed and paid deal from a tagged cohort, with the cohort period and size stated
the model states, for each channel, the cash-out to cash-in lag as well as the ratio chain
no ratio in the model comes from outside the operator's own records
revisit_triggers: a completed cohort reaching final payment, which closes the chain for the first time or updates it
a compensation change that alters net per deal and therefore allowable acquisition cost
a measured shift in any stage ratio beyond its normal variation

nodes.definition: When results fall, determine which stage actually broke before spending money on a fix, because the leads are bad is the most common and least examined explanation in this business and it is wrong about half the time. The diagnosis is positional and reads the ratio chain from the front: a collapse in contact rate points at the record itself - its age, phone accuracy, resale history, consent provenance, or the number of buyers it was shared with - and not at the person calling; a healthy contact rate with a collapsed sit rate points at the appointment-setting conversation, at the mismatch between what the advertisement implied and what the seller actually sells, or at appointments being set without the decision-makers present; healthy sits with poor closes point at loose qualification upstream, at proposal quality, or at the seller's own process in the room; and healthy closes followed by heavy post-signature attrition points at what was said in the room, which is the operator's own conduct rather than anyone's leads. Diagnosis requires per-source tagging, honest disposition codes, and a cohort large enough to distinguish a pattern from a bad fortnight, because small samples over-read normal variation and produce confident wrong conclusions. The two classic wastes are rotating vendors on a sample too small to mean anything, and retraining a representative whose leads were weeks old and sold four ways.

included: locating the break by stage across contact, sit, close and post-signature survival
the sample-size discipline that separates pattern from variance
the classic misattributions and their cost
excluded: the appointment-setting and presentation scripts themselves as content
the proposal's own quality and integrity, which belong to the sibling proposal knowledge base
any benchmark for what a healthy rate should be, which is the operator's own history

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a sustained move in a stage ratio, or a controlled change to one input whose cohort effect can be read

pros.claim: Positional diagnosis directs the fix at the stage that actually broke, which is usually cheaper than the fix the operator would have bought
pros.example: finding that the sit rate fell after an advertisement changed, rather than paying to replace a lead vendor whose records were unchanged

pros.claim: It protects representatives from being blamed for a supply problem, which is a real retention issue in commission-only sales teams
pros.example: showing a discouraged representative that contact rate, not their calling, fell when the vendor started reselling aged records

cons.claim: Diagnosis needs volume that a small operator may not have, so honest answers are often not available inside the month the problem hurts
cons.example: a two-week slump that cannot be distinguished from ordinary variance until another month of data exists

cons.claim: Stages interact, so a single-stage explanation can mislead when two causes move together
cons.example: an ad change that both lowers lead intent and shifts the households reached, degrading contact and sit rates at once

failure_modes: declaring the leads bad without checking contact rate against the vendor's baseline
changing script, vendor, and territory simultaneously so nothing can be attributed
acting on a sample too small to distinguish from noise
letting disposition codes be chosen for appearance rather than accuracy
acceptance_tests: each investigation names the stage where the ratio moved and the evidence for it before any corrective spend is committed
one change at a time is made and the affected cohort is tagged so the effect can be read
revisit_triggers: any stage ratio moving beyond its normal variation for consecutive periods
a vendor, advertisement, script, or territory change
a representative reporting that lead quality has changed

nodes.definition: Order the homeowner screens so the cheapest disqualifier runs first and no expensive step is ever spent on a project that cannot close, and make each gate produce an explicit outcome rather than an impression. The sequence, executed at screening depth rather than proposal depth, runs: is this person actually an owner and a decision-maker, including co-owners, a spouse, a trust, an estate, an HOA layer, or a landlord who is not present; do they intend to keep the property long enough for a long-term commitment to make sense; is there enough electricity consumption for a system to be worth proposing at all; are there obvious site red flags such as roof age or condition, dominant shade, a roof type the partner installer will not work on, or a service panel that visibly needs attention; and only then, is the household in a position to finance the commitment. Each gate has a defined pass, a defined fail, and a defined not-yet, and a fail ends the process politely and immediately rather than being carried forward in hope, because a carried-forward fail is how sunk lead cost turns into pressure at the close. The gates deliberately stop at screening depth: the full consumption analysis against the utility rate schedule, orientation, tilt, shade modelling, offset design, and production estimation that produce a real proposal belong to the sibling proposal-side knowledge base, and this sequence exists precisely so that work is only ever spent on households that can proceed.

included: the gate order and the cost logic behind it
ownership, decision authority and tenure intent as the first gate
pass, fail and not-yet outcomes per gate with an immediate end on fail
the screening-depth boundary and the handoff to proposal work
excluded: proposal-depth consumption, rate-schedule, orientation, shade and production analysis, which belong to the sibling proposal knowledge base
the financing structures themselves and their comparison
any promise about what a system would produce or save

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a rise in disqualifying facts discovered at or after the appointment, or a change in what the installer partner will build

pros.claim: Front-loading the cheapest disqualifier protects the operator's scarcest resource, which is time in front of qualified households
pros.example: one ownership question on the first call ending a conversation that would otherwise have consumed an evening appointment and a proposal

pros.claim: Explicit not-yet outcomes keep genuine future business alive without pretending it is present business
pros.example: a household two years from a planned roof replacement re-contacted deliberately rather than pushed now or forgotten entirely

cons.claim: Hard screening lowers appointment volume, which looks like underperformance to anyone measuring activity rather than installed deals
cons.example: a representative with half the appointments of a peer and more installs, judged badly on a set-appointment metric

cons.claim: Gates applied mechanically can discard a household whose situation the screening question was too coarse to capture
cons.example: a co-owner absent from the first call being treated as a fail rather than a scheduling problem

failure_modes: booking an appointment before ownership and decision authority are established
running the expensive screens before the cheap ones because the conversation is going well
converting a fail into a maybe to protect the month's number
letting the screening drift into proposal-depth analysis that the seller is not positioned to do
acceptance_tests: every appointment record shows the gates that were passed, with an outcome recorded per gate rather than a general impression
no proposal-depth work is commissioned for a household with an unresolved gate
