nodes.definition: Establish from the homeowner's own utility record, and never from an assumption about house size or neighbourhood, whether there is enough electricity consumption to justify building a proposal at all. At screening depth this means obtaining a full twelve months of usage - the bill history in the homeowner's own utility portal, a data-access authorization where the utility offers one, or at minimum a set of bills covering both a peak and a trough month - and reading it for three things only: total annual consumption, the seasonal shape, and any known change ahead such as an electric vehicle, a heat pump, a pool, a home addition, a new baby, or a household member moving out. Reading a single month is the classic screening error, because it treats a peak or a trough as the year and produces a conversation the proposal will later have to contradict. Low consumption is a legitimate and common disqualifier and should be said plainly rather than solved by enlarging assumptions about future usage; a genuinely planned future load is a not-yet, not a licence to size around a hope. The screen deliberately stops short of the rate-schedule analysis, offset design, and production modelling that produce a real proposal - those belong to the sibling proposal knowledge base - and it answers exactly one question: is it worth anyone's time to proceed.

included: obtaining twelve months of the homeowner's own usage and how to get it
reading annual total, seasonal shape, and known upcoming load changes
low consumption as a legitimate disqualifier
the boundary at which the proposal-side analysis takes over
excluded: rate-schedule analysis, tariff comparison, offset design and production modelling, which belong to the sibling proposal knowledge base
any statement of what a system would produce or save for this household
estimating usage from house size, occupancy, or neighbourhood when the record is available

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a household load change reported after screening, or a proposal-stage consumption picture that contradicts the screen

pros.claim: Working from the homeowner's own twelve-month record makes every later number defensible and visibly not invented
pros.example: opening the utility portal with the homeowner and reading the year together rather than quoting a typical household figure

pros.claim: A consumption screen kills the most expensive category of dead deal early, the household that likes the idea but has nothing to offset
pros.example: ending a friendly conversation before a proposal is commissioned because the annual total is plainly too low

cons.claim: Getting twelve months of data requires the homeowner to act, and some will not, which loses households that might have qualified
cons.example: a homeowner who cannot recall portal credentials and declines to retrieve them, ending an otherwise viable conversation

cons.claim: The screen reads the past, while the household lives in the future, so genuinely planned load changes sit uncomfortably between honest and speculative
cons.example: an electric vehicle the household intends to buy next year, which is real but not yet in any record

failure_modes: screening on one summer or one winter bill
estimating usage from house size when the record could have been obtained
sizing around a hoped-for future load to keep a marginal household alive
carrying a low-consumption household forward as a maybe rather than disqualifying it
acceptance_tests: the record for each proceeding household shows twelve months of usage or an explicit stated reason why a shorter record was accepted
any assumed future load change is recorded as an assumption attributable to the homeowner rather than presented as current usage
revisit_triggers: the homeowner reports a household or load change after screening
a proposal returns a consumption picture materially different from the screen
the utility changes how usage data is made available to homeowners

nodes.definition: Catch at the doorstep or on the first call the physical conditions that will either kill the project later or quietly turn it into a different, more expensive project the homeowner never agreed to. The red-flag set is deliberately coarse because it is a screen and not an assessment: a roof near the end of its serviceable life or with active leaks, since building an array over it means paying to remove and reinstall that array within the financing term; roof materials, ages, or structures a given installer partner will not work on or will surcharge heavily; permanent heavy shade from mature trees or an adjacent building that no design will engineer away; an electrical service panel that visibly needs replacement or upgrading before anything can be connected; ground-mount ambitions with trenching, setback, or soil questions; and any historic-district, homeowners-association, shared-roof, or condominium condition that adds an approval nobody has budgeted time for. The correct response to a red flag is to name it out loud, say who resolves it and roughly at whose cost as a category rather than as a quoted figure, and then either sequence it - roof first, then solar - or disqualify. Detailed shade, orientation, tilt, and production modelling is not performed here and no production or savings consequence is asserted; this screen only decides whether a proposal is worth building and warns the homeowner early about a cost they would otherwise meet late and badly.

included: the coarse red-flag list covering roof condition, material, shade, service panel, mount type and approval layers
naming the flag to the homeowner and sequencing or disqualifying
the installer partner's own build constraints as an input to the screen
excluded: shade, orientation, tilt and production modelling and any resulting production or savings figure, which belong to the sibling proposal knowledge base
structural, electrical, or roofing assessment, which requires the relevant licensed trade
quoting a price for roof work, panel upgrade, or tree removal

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: survey findings that the screen missed, or a change in what the installer partner will build on

pros.claim: Naming a roof or panel problem at first contact converts the seller from someone selling into someone advising, which is the position referrals come from
pros.example: telling a homeowner their roof should be addressed before any array goes on it, and being the person they call when it is

pros.claim: Early red-flag capture prevents the most damaging late failure, a survey that changes the project after the homeowner has already committed
pros.example: a service-panel condition identified at the door rather than discovered at survey and added to the price afterwards

cons.claim: A coarse screen produces false positives that discard workable sites, since only a survey can settle several of these questions
cons.example: an aged but sound roof treated as disqualifying when the installer would have accepted it

cons.claim: Sequencing a household behind roof work usually loses it to whoever is present when the roof is finally replaced
cons.example: a homeowner who replaces the roof eighteen months later and signs with the company that happened to be at the door that week

failure_modes: seeing a roof or panel problem and leaving it for the survey to raise
quoting or estimating roof, tree, or electrical work the seller is not licensed to price
drifting from screening into an assessment that only a licensed trade can make
ignoring an approval layer such as an association or historic district until permitting
acceptance_tests: each proceeding household has a recorded red-flag screen naming any flag found and the sequencing or disqualification decision taken
no roof, structural, or electrical cost is quoted by the seller; flags are handed to the appropriate licensed trade or to the installer
revisit_triggers: a survey finding a condition the screen should have caught
a change of installer partner with different build constraints
a rise in projects re-priced or cancelled after survey

nodes.definition: Determine whether a household can plausibly reach an approval before anyone designs anything, while staying strictly inside the seller's lane. The screen runs through the financing partner's own prequalification path - the lender's or provider's soft-inquiry prequalification, initiated and completed by the homeowner themselves - rather than through the seller collecting, storing, or interpreting credit information; the seller's role is to explain that a prequalification step exists, that it belongs to the lender, what documentation that class of product typically asks for as a category, such as identity, evidence of property ownership, and evidence of income, and then to accept the lender's answer without editorializing. Several adjacent facts decide feasibility and are worth surfacing at the same time: whether the property is held in a trust or an estate and who is legally able to sign; whether every title holder will in fact sign; whether a structure that depends on a tax position assumes something about the household that only their own tax adviser can confirm; and whether an existing mortgage, lien, or shared-roof arrangement complicates the paperwork that a financing structure may require. The seller never advises on credit repair, tax position, or which structure is best for a household, never runs or stores a credit inquiry itself, and never characterizes a declined prequalification as anything other than the lender's decision - the explanation and comparison of cash, loan, lease, and power-purchase structures belongs to the sibling financing-literacy knowledge base and the decision belongs to the homeowner and their own advisors.

included: routing prequalification through the lender's own soft-inquiry path run by the homeowner
documentation categories the product class typically requires
title, trust, estate and co-signer facts that decide feasibility
the advice and data-handling boundaries the seller does not cross
excluded: explaining or comparing cash, loan, lease and power-purchase structures, which belongs to the sibling financing-literacy knowledge base
any credit, tax, legal, or insurance advice, including whether a household can use a tax credit
the seller collecting, storing, or interpreting credit data or running an inquiry

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a financing partner changing its prequalification path or product classes, or a pattern of projects failing verification after passing the screen

pros.claim: A lender-run prequalification gives a real answer without the seller ever touching credit data, which removes both a data-security burden and a class of complaint
pros.example: sending the homeowner the lender's own prequalification link and never seeing a score or a report

pros.claim: Surfacing title and trust facts early prevents the failure that appears at the worst possible moment, when documents cannot be signed by the person who agreed
pros.example: learning at screening that the property sits in a family trust with a co-trustee who has never been part of the conversation

cons.claim: Raising financing early can feel intrusive and ends conversations with households that would have engaged once they saw the numbers
cons.example: a homeowner declining a prequalification step before any proposal exists and disengaging entirely

cons.claim: The strict advice boundary leaves homeowners with real questions the seller is not permitted to answer, which can read as evasive if not explained
cons.example: a homeowner asking whether they will benefit from a tax credit and receiving a referral to their own tax adviser instead of an answer

failure_modes: collecting credit information directly or running an inquiry on the homeowner's behalf
characterizing a lender decline as the homeowner's fault or speculating about the reason
advising on which structure is best, or on tax benefit, to keep a deal alive
proceeding to design while a title, trust, or co-signer question is unresolved
acceptance_tests: no credit data is collected, stored, or interpreted by the seller, and prequalification is evidenced as having been run by the homeowner through the provider's own path
the record shows title holders, trust or estate status, and who will sign, resolved before design work is commissioned
no tax, legal, or financial recommendation appears in any homeowner-facing communication from the seller
revisit_triggers: a financing partner changes its prequalification path, documentation requirements, or product classes
a project fails at financing verification after passing the screen
a homeowner asks a question that sits outside the advice boundary

nodes.definition: Make the conversation in which the seller says this is not right for you a normal, practised, scripted part of the job rather than an admission of failure, because in a channel carrying this much accumulated suspicion the demonstrated willingness to disqualify is simultaneously the ethical core of the business and the strongest generator of the introductions it runs on. The practice has a shape: name the specific reason drawn from the screens in plain language - the consumption is too low to justify a commitment this long, the roof needs replacing before anything goes on it, the household is moving inside the horizon, the lender's prequalification did not pass and pushing further would only cost the homeowner - then offer the constructive next step where one honestly exists, such as getting the roof quoted or returning after the panel work, leave the relationship intact and the door explicitly open, and record the disqualification reason so that the channel, the advertisement, and the setting script that produced this misfit can be corrected upstream. The cost must be accepted openly rather than minimized: the walk-away destroys a sunk lead cost, an evening, and sometimes the month's number, and it arrives at precisely the moment when the quota, the money already spent, and the operator's own cash-flow gap all argue against the homeowner. That is exactly why the rule is set in advance, scripted, and audited afterwards, rather than decided in the room by a tired person with a number to hit.

included: the scripted walk-away and its plain-language reasons
the constructive next step and the deliberately open door
recording the disqualification reason as an upstream correction signal
explicit acceptance of the cost and the reason the rule is pre-committed
excluded: the reputation and referral engine built from completed installs, which belongs to the sibling installer-partnership and reputation knowledge base
advising the homeowner on what they should do instead beyond naming the obvious next trade or question
retention or save attempts applied to a homeowner exercising a cancellation right

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a fall in recorded disqualification rate under quota pressure, or clustering of disqualification reasons on one upstream source

pros.claim: A disqualification delivered well converts a lost deal into the most credible endorsement available in this market
pros.example: a homeowner who was told not to buy recommending the seller to a neighbour whose situation is different

pros.claim: Recorded disqualification reasons feed the upstream fix, turning individual walk-aways into channel and script corrections
pros.example: a cluster of moving-soon disqualifications tracing back to one lead source targeting a transient area

cons.claim: The practice destroys real, already-spent acquisition cost with nothing recovered, and does so most often in the months the operator can least afford it
cons.example: walking away from a purchased and worked lead in a slow month with no offsetting deal behind it

cons.claim: Disqualification judgement can be wrong, and a household turned away on a coarse screen may have been workable with more effort
cons.example: declining a household on a roof concern the installer would have accepted after a survey

failure_modes: softening a fail into a follow-up to avoid recording a loss
disqualifying silently by going quiet rather than telling the homeowner plainly
handing the household to another representative to try a harder approach
failing to record the reason, so the upstream cause is never corrected
acceptance_tests: every ended conversation carries a recorded disqualification reason drawn from a named gate rather than a generic not-interested code
disqualified households were told the reason in plain language and, where one existed, a constructive next step
no disqualified household is re-worked by another representative without a changed fact recorded
revisit_triggers: disqualification reasons clustering on one channel, advertisement, or setter
pressure on the number producing a fall in recorded disqualifications
a disqualified household later installing with a competitor without any fact having changed

nodes.definition: Define the pipeline as a set of verifiable states with explicit evidence-based exit criteria, because in residential solar the sale does not end at signature and a business that measures only closed is blind to most of its own risk and all of its own timing. A workable stage set runs: lead created with its source tagged; contact made; appointment set; appointment held with the decision-makers present; proposal presented; agreement signed; financing verified and approved; site survey completed; design and engineering finished; permit submitted and approved; installation scheduled; installed; inspection passed; permission to operate granted by the utility; and finally, commission paid with the last clawback window expired. Each stage advances only on evidence - a dated document, a portal status, a confirmation from the party responsible - never on a representative's optimism, and each stage carries its own characteristic stall causes and its own cancellation risk. The structural fact this model exists to expose is that the seller's control effectively ends somewhere around financing approval, while the seller's money does not arrive until several stages later that belong to the installer, the authority having jurisdiction, and the utility. The operational management of that post-signature period, the homeowner communication through it, and the partnership work behind install timelines belong to the sibling installer-partnership knowledge base; this model exists so that pipeline mathematics, income expectation, and cancellation analysis all count the same real states.

included: the full stage list from lead created to final payment with clawback expiry
evidence-based exit criteria per stage
the point at which seller control ends and other parties' timelines begin
excluded: managing the post-signature period with the installer and the homeowner, which belongs to the sibling installer-partnership knowledge base
the permitting and interconnection process itself, which belongs to the sibling proposal and process knowledge base
any assertion of how long a stage takes, which is measured per market and per partner

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change of partner, provider, or jurisdiction that alters the stage set, or repeated stalling in a stage the model does not separate

pros.claim: Evidence-based stages make the pipeline countable, which is the precondition for every forecast and every diagnosis in this knowledge base
pros.example: an appointment counted as held only when the decision-makers were actually present, which changes the sit rate the whole model runs on

pros.claim: Explicit post-signature stages surface the risk that a signature-focused business never sees until the reversal arrives
pros.example: a cohort visibly accumulating in the permit stage months before the income shortfall it implies

cons.claim: Most of the stages are updated by other parties, so stage data quality depends on partner systems the seller does not control
cons.example: an installer portal whose status lags reality by days, making stage timestamps approximate

cons.claim: A detailed stage model invites administrative effort that competes directly with selling time
cons.example: a representative updating fifteen stage fields instead of making calls

failure_modes: advancing a stage on a representative's expectation rather than on evidence
collapsing the post-signature stages into one installed bucket that hides where deals actually stall
counting set appointments as held
keeping no dates, so lag time is never measurable
acceptance_tests: each stage has a written exit criterion naming the evidence that advances it, and stage changes carry dates
post-signature stages are tracked individually rather than as a single bucket
held appointments are distinguished from set appointments in every count
revisit_triggers: a change of installer partner, financing provider, or permitting jurisdiction that changes the stage set
deals repeatedly stalling in a stage the model does not separate
a stage whose evidence source becomes unavailable or unreliable

nodes.definition: Maintain the record layer without which every other number in this knowledge base is a guess dressed as a figure: one record per homeowner, created at first touch rather than at first interest, carrying the channel and the specific source it came from, the consent artifact and its timestamp, every stage transition with its date, appointments distinguished between set and held, an honest disposition code when the conversation ends including the named disqualification reason, and the compensation milestone status of anything signed. The discipline is behavioural rather than technical - a simple system used consistently beats an elaborate one filled in on Friday afternoons - and its enemies are familiar: the untagged lead that arrived from somewhere nobody recorded, the deal that lives only in one representative's phone and leaves with them, the still-thinking-about-it that never resolves into anything countable, and the disposition code chosen to make a week look better than it was. Two obligations ride on the same records and raise their stakes: contact-consent and opt-out evidence must be retrievable per homeowner for the period the applicable rules require, and the disqualification record is what allows the honesty rules of this business to be audited rather than merely asserted. These records contain personal information about households and are stored, access-limited, and disposed of accordingly.

included: one record per homeowner created at first touch with channel and specific source
consent artifact, stage timestamps, set-versus-held appointments, disposition and disqualification codes, milestone status
retrievability of consent and opt-out evidence
handling records as personal information
excluded: choice of a particular software product or vendor
the installer's own project management records after handoff, which belong to the sibling installer-partnership knowledge base
any use of the records for a purpose the homeowner was not told about

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an unanswerable channel or consent question, a personnel or system change, or a change in applicable retention obligations

pros.claim: Source tagging and stage timestamps are the entire evidentiary basis of the economic model, and they cost almost nothing if captured at intake
pros.example: being able to attribute installed deals to one specific advertisement rather than to a whole channel

pros.claim: Retrievable consent and opt-out evidence turns a contact dispute from an existential problem into a lookup
pros.example: answering a homeowner's complaint with the timestamped enquiry and the disclosure language they saw

cons.claim: Record discipline is unpaid work that competes with selling time and degrades first in exactly the busy periods whose data matters most
cons.example: a strong month recorded so thinly that its channel economics can never be reconstructed

cons.claim: Holding household personal information creates a security and retention obligation a small operator must actually meet
cons.example: consent records and usage data sitting in an unsecured shared spreadsheet accessible to former representatives

failure_modes: creating records only for interested homeowners, which destroys every denominator
letting a representative keep the pipeline in a personal phone or notebook
using disposition codes cosmetically rather than honestly
retaining personal data indefinitely with no access control or disposal rule
acceptance_tests: every lead has a record created at first touch with channel and specific source, with no untagged intake path
consent artifact, stage dates, held-versus-set appointment status, and disposition reason are present and retrievable per homeowner
access to household records is limited and a retention and disposal rule is written and applied
revisit_triggers: a representative joining or leaving, or a change of system
an inability to answer a channel or consent question from the records
a change in the retention or data-protection obligations that apply

nodes.definition: Work backwards from a target number of installed and fully paid projects in a future month to the volume of leads and held appointments that must exist today, using the operator's own stage survival ratios and - the part almost everyone omits - the operator's own stage lag times. Because the residential cycle from signature to permission to operate is long and variable, the pipeline producing income in a given month was built months earlier, so a seller who reacts to a thin month by working harder inside that month has already missed the window that determined it; the correct response was to have kept lead input steady through the good months when the temptation to coast was strongest. The mathematics is therefore a chain of survival ratios applied to a lag-shifted cohort rather than a single close rate applied to a monthly lead count, and it must be recomputed whenever a ratio or a lag moves. Two structural properties fall out of it and both are counterintuitive: the required lead input is substantially higher than a naive close-rate calculation suggests once post-signature attrition is included, and steady moderate input beats bursts, because a burst creates appointment demand beyond the seller's capacity to hold appointments well and then leaves a hole in the following quarter that no amount of effort inside that quarter can fill.

included: backwards sizing from an installed-deal target through survival ratios and stage lags
the build-ahead principle and the capacity limit on bursts
recomputation when a ratio or lag moves
excluded: any supplied conversion ratio, lag length, or benchmark
installer capacity planning and install scheduling, which belong to the installer and the sibling partnership knowledge base
sales-team compensation or quota design

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a material move in a stage ratio or lag, an installer or permitting timeline change, or a change in selling capacity

pros.claim: Backwards sizing makes the true cost of a quiet prospecting week visible at the moment it happens rather than a quarter later
pros.example: seeing that a fortnight of no lead input maps directly onto a specific month with no installs

pros.claim: Lag-aware planning removes the strongest structural driver of pressure selling, the attempt to rescue a month from inside it
pros.example: responding to a weak forecast by raising input now for a later month instead of pushing marginal households to sign this week

cons.claim: The model needs stable ratios and lags that a young or small business does not yet have, so early versions are estimates that can mislead confidently
cons.example: sizing a quarter on a close rate derived from a handful of appointments

cons.claim: Steady input costs money in months when nothing is arriving, which is precisely when spending feels least defensible
cons.example: maintaining lead spend through a slow stretch while the current month's income is already determined

failure_modes: applying a single close rate to a monthly lead count and ignoring lag entirely
cutting lead spend in a thin month and creating the next thin quarter
buying a burst of leads that exceeds appointment capacity and burning them
planning against signed deals rather than against deals that survive to payment
acceptance_tests: the current forward plan states, for a named future month, the required leads and held appointments now and the ratios and lags used
the plan is recomputed when any stage ratio or lag moves materially, with the revision dated
revisit_triggers: a stage ratio or lag moving beyond its normal variation
an installer backlog or permitting timeline change that lengthens the cycle
a capacity change such as adding or losing a representative

nodes.definition: Carry cancellation as a modelled input to every economic decision rather than as an unpleasant surprise, because in this vertical a signed agreement is a probability and not a receipt. The population of signed-but-never-installed projects has distinct causes that behave differently and must be counted separately: rescission inside the cooling-off window; financing that fails at verification after a prequalification passed; survey findings that change the design, the price, or the feasibility; permit or interconnection refusal; an install queue long enough that the homeowner cools off, is re-sold by a competitor, or simply moves; and buyer's remorse following a sale the homeowner never fully understood - the last being the only cause the seller's own conduct fully controls, and therefore the one whose rate is the single best quantitative test of whether the anti-pressure identity is real. The modelling work is to measure the rate by cause and by lead channel, apply it to cost per installed deal so channel comparisons stop flattering the channels that sign easily and cancel often, apply it to commission expectation so income planning uses expected rather than signed value, and read the by-cause breakdown as a feedback signal into qualification, conduct, and channel mix. The operational work of preventing, communicating through, and administering cancellations and their clawbacks with the installer belongs to the sibling installer-partnership knowledge base; here cancellation is an economic input and a diagnostic mirror.

included: the cause taxonomy of signed-but-never-installed projects
measuring rate by cause and by channel and applying it to cost and to expected commission
remorse-driven cancellation as the quantitative test of the conduct rules
excluded: the operational prevention, communication and administration of cancellations and clawbacks with the installer, which belong to the sibling installer-partnership knowledge base
any supplied cancellation rate or benchmark
retention pressure applied to a homeowner exercising a lawful cancellation right

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in overall cancellation rate or cause mix, or an install, permitting, or interconnection change that alters the exposure window

pros.claim: Cancellation-adjusted economics reverses channel rankings that raw close rates get exactly backwards
pros.example: a channel with the best close rate ranking last once the deals that never reached installation are removed

pros.claim: Splitting cancellations by cause turns a discouraging number into an actionable one, and gives the conduct rules a measurable proxy
pros.example: a rise in remorse cancellations concentrated on one representative, visible before any complaint is filed

cons.claim: Most causes lie outside the seller's control, so a correct model can still deliver an outcome no amount of selling skill could have changed
cons.example: an interconnection refusal reversing a project the seller executed impeccably

cons.claim: Cause attribution depends on honest coding by the person closest to the loss, who has an obvious incentive to code it as external
cons.example: a remorse cancellation recorded as an install-delay cancellation

failure_modes: planning income on signed value rather than expected value
treating all cancellations as one undifferentiated rate and losing the diagnostic
coding remorse cancellations as external causes
responding to a lawful cancellation with retention pressure rather than processing and learning from it
acceptance_tests: cancellation is measured by cause and by lead channel, and the current rates are applied in both the cost-per-installed-deal figure and the income forecast
the remorse-driven share is tracked separately by representative and reviewed against the conduct rules
revisit_triggers: a rise in overall cancellation or a shift in its cause mix
an install backlog, permitting, or interconnection change that alters the exposure window
a new representative, channel, or financing product entering the mix

edges.why_related: the position is chosen to be operable under the conduct rules rather than the rules being fitted to whatever position pays most
which registration and permit classes attach depends entirely on whether the operator sells, dealers, or only introduces
canvassing permits and per-person registrations are the gate through which the door channel becomes lawful at all
the in-home solicitation context is where vulnerability signals appear and where the procedural duty has to be executed
which compensation mechanism applies - spread, percentage, flat, or referral fee - follows from the position taken
the milestone and clawback map is drawn against the same agreement whose arithmetic the literacy work reconstructs
whether the operator pays introducers, receives introduction fees, or both is determined by the position occupied
the reserve rule and the runway horizon are computed directly from the milestone timing and the clawback trigger list
who owns the lead record and who funds acquisition decides which channels are even available to the operator
each channel activates a different contact-consent obligation class, so the channel set determines the compliance set
the ratio chain is computed per channel and per source, so the tagged channel set is its unit of analysis
diagnosis reads the same stage ratios the economics model computes, and cannot run before they exist
the gates exist to make honest non-fit findings early, which is the conduct rule expressed as process
the consumption screen is one gate in the ordered sequence and runs only after ownership and tenure pass
the site red-flag screen is the gate that follows consumption and precedes any financing step
the gates define what counts as a qualified opportunity entering the countable stages
the record layer stores exactly the stage transitions and dates the stage model defines
survival ratios and stage lags can only be computed from dated, tagged records
the clawback trigger list is the same event list the cancellation cause taxonomy has to count
where a vulnerability signal is present the walk-away is not optional and cannot be traded for a deferred signature
a vendor that cannot produce consent artifacts is unusable regardless of price, so the compliance class bounds the supplier set
who may lawfully be paid for procuring a home-improvement contract is defined by the same licensing regime
a stage may only advance on evidence, which forbids advancing a homeowner through pressure to make the pipeline look healthier
permits, do-not-knock registries and hour limits bound where and when the canvassing channel can be run at all
acquisition cost already spent on a lead argues for converting it, while the screens argue for ending the conversation
edges.resolution_rule: the screen result wins without exception; the acquisition cost is sunk and is dealt with by re-rating or retiring the channel that produced the misfit, never by pushing the household

edges.why_related: a personal cash-flow gap near a milestone creates direct pressure to close a household that should not be closed
edges.resolution_rule: the conduct rules dominate absolutely; a cash-flow gap is answered by reserve, by earlier pipeline input, or by reducing fixed cost, and never by a faster close or a suspended rule

edges.why_related: a forward volume target tempts the operator to loosen the gates so more households enter the countable stages
edges.resolution_rule: the gates stay fixed and the shortfall is met by raising lead input or changing channel mix; if input cannot be raised, the forecast is lowered rather than the gate

edges.why_related: a spread mechanism pays the seller more the higher the homeowner is priced, which is structurally opposed to pricing the household honestly
edges.resolution_rule: price is set by a stated, consistent rule the seller can defend to any homeowner rather than by what a household appears able to bear; where the compensation design makes that impossible, the position or partner is changed rather than the pricing behaviour

edges.why_related: the measured cancellation rate by cause is the input that sizes the reserve and sets expected rather than signed income
the cooling-off right creates a structural early-cancellation population that exists independently of anything the seller does afterwards
households ended honestly before signing do not appear later as remorse cancellations and clawbacks
both are homeowner-protection duties executed in the same in-home moment and audited from the same visit record
the intrusive financing step is only worth asking a household to take once consumption has shown the project is worth proposing
source tags, stage dates and honest dispositions must be in place before any diagnosis of a falling ratio is possible
diagnosis results feed back into the mix, retiring a channel or fixing the stage that actually broke rather than replacing the supplier reflexively
the cancellation cause mix names which gate was too loose and tightens it, so post-signature losses become screening improvements
the remorse-driven share of cancellations is the quantitative audit of whether the conduct rules are actually being followed in the room

conflict_axes.name: close_in_the_room_versus_homeowner_pace
conflict_axes.description: Every mechanic that raises same-visit close rate - the expiring price, the manufactured deadline, the reluctance to leave without a signature - also produces the remorse cancellations, complaints, and reputational damage this vertical is already known for.
poles: close while you are in the room
let the homeowner decide at their own pace
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the pace belongs to the homeowner without exception; the only legitimate accelerator is better preparation - the usage record obtained in advance, the decision-makers present, the questions anticipated

conflict_axes.name: lead_volume_versus_lead_quality
conflict_axes.description: Shared, aged, and co-registered records are cheap per unit and abundant, while exclusive, consent-verified, high-intent supply is scarce and expensive per unit; the two look opposite on the invoice and often reverse once installed-deal cost is computed.
poles: buy volume and work the numbers
buy quality and work fewer households properly
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: let cancellation-adjusted cost per installed deal decide, but treat consent provenance and a workable return policy as qualifying conditions that no price advantage can override

conflict_axes.name: spread_pay_versus_honest_pricing
conflict_axes.description: A spread or percentage mechanism pays the seller more the higher the homeowner is priced, which places the compensation design in direct structural tension with the verified-numbers identity rather than merely tempting a weak individual.
poles: price to what the household will accept
price by a consistent defensible rule
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: adopt a stated pricing rule the seller could show any homeowner and apply it uniformly; where the compensation design makes a defensible rule impossible, change the partner or the position rather than the pricing behaviour

conflict_axes.name: sunk_acquisition_cost_versus_disqualification
conflict_axes.description: The moment a screen fails is the moment the money already spent on that lead argues hardest for continuing, and the argument is strongest in the months the operator can least afford to lose a deal.
poles: recover the acquisition cost by converting
end the conversation on the screen result
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the screen result is final and the cost is sunk; the correct response is to re-rate or retire the channel that produced the misfit, and to record the disqualification reason so the upstream cause is fixed

conflict_axes.name: cash_now_versus_clawback_safety
conflict_axes.description: Milestone advances arrive when the operator needs money most, but they remain reversible for months, so treating them as income funds the business with money that may have to be returned.
poles: spend advances as they arrive
hold advances until the last trigger expires
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold clawbackable receipts as a separate balance released only at trigger expiry, and size the reserve from the operator's own measured attrition rather than from optimism

conflict_axes.name: control_versus_capital_in_position_choice
conflict_axes.description: The dealer position gives pricing control, lead ownership, and the largest share of the value, and demands the capital and cancellation absorption that the representative and referral positions avoid at the cost of controlling almost nothing.
poles: own the sales organization and its economics
carry no capital and accept a thin defined fee
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: choose against the operator's actual runway and risk tolerance rather than against the headline per-deal number, and revisit the choice only on a deliberate schedule rather than after a bad month

conflict_axes.name: canvass_reach_versus_neighbourhood_reputation
conflict_axes.description: Door canvassing reaches households no other channel touches and simultaneously spends the local goodwill that the referral flow - the only compounding asset in this vertical - is built from.
poles: work the doors for reach
protect the neighbourhood relationship
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: run the door channel only under the full conduct and permit rules with audited crews, and measure it on installed deals and complaint rate together rather than on appointments set

conflict_axes.name: screening_depth_versus_appointment_throughput
conflict_axes.description: Hard screening on the phone produces fewer, better appointments and looks like underperformance on any activity metric; loose screening fills the calendar with appointments that consume evenings and produce disqualifications in the room.
poles: screen hard and book less
book everything and screen in person
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the gates fixed and judge representatives on installed deals per working week rather than on appointments set; if volume must rise, raise lead input rather than lower the gate

conflict_axes.name: jurisdiction_certainty_versus_expansion_speed
conflict_axes.description: Verifying registrations, canvass permits, contact rules and referral-compensation classes town by town is slow and repetitive, while the pipeline and the crew are ready to work the next town this weekend.
poles: expand where demand appears
sell only where obligations are verified
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: no territory opens before its obligation register is complete and dated; expansion is scheduled against verification lead time rather than against enthusiasm

conflict_axes.name: record_discipline_versus_selling_time
conflict_axes.description: Every minute spent tagging sources, dating stage transitions, and coding dispositions honestly is a minute not spent in front of a household, and the discipline degrades first in the busy periods whose data would have been most informative.
poles: maximize time in front of homeowners
maintain the records the economics depend on
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the record set minimal but non-negotiable - source, consent artifact, stage dates, held-versus-set, disposition reason, milestone status - and capture it at the moment of the event rather than in a weekly catch-up

edge_cases.description: The person at the table is one of several title holders, or the property is held in a trust or an estate, and the other signatories have never been part of the conversation
edge_cases.trigger: a household proceeds toward signing with an absent co-owner, co-trustee, or executor
edge_cases.mitigation: resolve title holders and signing authority at the first gate, require every signatory to be present for the presentation rather than only for signature, and treat an absent signatory as a scheduling problem rather than a fail

edge_cases.description: A homeowner from a purchased list states they never requested any contact about solar
edge_cases.trigger: a contacted homeowner disputes the consent that the lead record claims
edge_cases.mitigation: stop contact immediately and add the household to the internal do-not-contact list, request the consent artifact from the vendor with its timestamp and originating page, and suspend the source until it is produced

edge_cases.description: A homeowner cancels inside the cooling-off window after a milestone advance has already been received and partly spent
edge_cases.trigger: a rescission arrives on a project whose first commission portion was advanced
edge_cases.mitigation: process the cancellation without any retention attempt, settle the reversal from the separately held clawbackable balance, and record the cause honestly so the remorse share stays visible

edge_cases.description: An elderly homeowner on a fixed income is enthusiastic and wants to sign tonight on a long-term financing commitment
edge_cases.trigger: a vulnerability signal appears alongside strong homeowner eagerness to sign immediately
edge_cases.mitigation: decline the same-visit signature regardless of the homeowner's insistence, offer to return with a family member or trusted advisor present, run the teach-back check, and disqualify if the obligation plainly displaces essentials

edge_cases.description: The roof is visibly at the end of its life and the homeowner refuses to address it before installing
edge_cases.trigger: a red-flag roof condition meets a homeowner who wants the array anyway
edge_cases.mitigation: state plainly that an array installed over a failing roof will have to be removed and reinstalled within the term, offer the sequenced path, and decline rather than proceed on the homeowner's acceptance of a cost they have not seen quantified by a roofer

edge_cases.description: A canvassing crew works a street covered by a municipal do-not-knock ordinance or without the required per-person permit
edge_cases.trigger: a route is worked before the territory's permit and registry position was verified
edge_cases.mitigation: stop the route immediately, record every household contacted, verify and obtain the required permissions before any return, and treat leads generated in the interval as unusable rather than as a windfall

edge_cases.description: A usage screen is run from a single summer bill and a proposal is built around a year that does not exist
edge_cases.trigger: a homeowner supplies one bill and the seller accepts it as representative
edge_cases.mitigation: require twelve months or an explicit peak-and-trough pair with the limitation recorded, and re-screen before any proposal work rather than after a homeowner notices the discrepancy

edge_cases.description: A shared lead is called by three sellers within minutes and the homeowner is already hostile when the fourth call arrives
edge_cases.trigger: a shared-supply record is delivered simultaneously to several buyers
edge_cases.mitigation: read the collapse at the contact and sit stage rather than blaming the caller, renegotiate exclusivity or delivery order, and price the sharing penalty into the channel's installed-deal cost before renewing

edge_cases.description: A satisfied homeowner offers to send neighbours in exchange for a payment, with no disclosure and no check on whether the arrangement is permitted
edge_cases.trigger: an informal paid-referral arrangement is proposed by a customer
edge_cases.mitigation: classify the arrangement, verify permissibility in the jurisdiction before agreeing to anything, document the trigger and timing in writing, and disclose the compensation in writing to every homeowner who arrives through it

edge_cases.description: The compensation plan, redline, or lead-source split changes while a pipeline signed under the previous terms is still working through installation
edge_cases.trigger: a mid-cycle amendment to the compensation agreement
edge_cases.mitigation: establish in writing which terms govern already-signed projects, recompute net per deal and allowable acquisition cost under both sets, and pause discretionary lead spend until the treatment is confirmed

edge_cases.description: The installer partner's backlog lengthens and signed projects sit for months before installation
edge_cases.trigger: install scheduling stretches beyond the homeowner's expectation set at signing
edge_cases.mitigation: re-model stage lags and the widened cancellation exposure, correct the timeline language used at the point of sale immediately, and lower income expectations rather than sell against a schedule that is no longer real

edge_cases.description: A homeowner asks directly whether they will get the tax credit and how much of it they will keep
edge_cases.trigger: a household seeks a personalized tax or financial conclusion from the seller
edge_cases.mitigation: explain that incentive eligibility depends on the household's own tax position, refer them to their own tax adviser, provide only the published description of the incentive class, and never model a household-specific benefit into a savings figure

workflow.action: Write the standing conduct rules before anything else is decided
workflow.description: Fix the traceable-number rule, the no-guarantee rule, the disclosed-principal rule, the no-manufactured-deadline rule, and the obligation to state a non-fit plainly, and make them binding on anyone who will sell under this name
workflow.artifact: written conduct standard with the rules stated as checkable behaviours
workflow.gate: each rule names an observable behaviour that an audit of a real appointment could confirm or refute, and applies explicitly to subcontracted canvassers

workflow.action: Choose the market position and record what it implies
workflow.description: Decide between commissioned representative, dealer, and referral partner against runway and risk tolerance, and record who owns the lead record, who funds acquisition, and who bears cancellation cost
workflow.gate: the three implications are stated and match a signed agreement rather than a conversation

workflow.description: Enumerate every seller-side registration, permit, and contact-related class for each jurisdiction to be sold into and verify each with the issuing authority
workflow.artifact: obligation register with authority, evidence, date and renewal per class per jurisdiction
workflow.gate: no territory is marked open without a complete dated register, and build-side licensing is recorded as the installer's obligation

workflow.action: Reconstruct the compensation arithmetic from the agreement
workflow.description: Derive from the signed compensation agreement the exact computation converting one project into one payment, including every modifier
workflow.artifact: worked one-project computation with each term traced to a clause
workflow.gate: the computation is produced from the agreement alone and is later reconciled line by line to the first statement

workflow.action: Map milestones, clawback triggers, and the reserve rule
workflow.description: Extract the payment stages, the full reversal trigger list, the recovery method, the reserve release condition, and the separation treatment
workflow.artifact: milestone and clawback map with a written reserve rule
workflow.gate: every trigger cites its clause and a separate clawbackable balance is established before the first deal is signed

workflow.action: Set the contact and door rules for every channel to be used
workflow.description: Define the consent basis, registry scrubbing, opt-out propagation, hours, recording position and retention for each intended channel, including door-derived contacts
workflow.artifact: contact-permission playbook with a per-lead consent artifact template
workflow.gate: each channel has a stated consent basis, a scrub step, and a retention rule, and an opt-out can be traced end to end in a test

workflow.action: Stand up the record layer before any money is spent on leads
workflow.description: Create the per-homeowner record with channel and specific source, consent artifact, stage dates, held-versus-set appointments, disposition and disqualification reasons, and milestone status
workflow.artifact: lead and pipeline record schema in the system actually used daily
workflow.gate: no intake path can create an untagged lead and every required field is capturable at the moment of its event

workflow.action: Select the starting channel mix with trial sizes and decision rules
workflow.description: Choose a small deliberate mix that the position and the conduct rules can support, with per-source tagging and a stated trial size and decision rule for each
workflow.artifact: channel plan with per-source tags, trial sizes and decision rules
workflow.gate: each channel's decision rule is expressed in cancellation-adjusted installed-deal cost, never in cost per lead

workflow.action: Qualify vendors before the first paid batch
workflow.description: Establish exclusivity, delivery order, return policy and window, lead age, resale history, consent artifacts and exit terms, then run a separately tagged trial batch
workflow.artifact: vendor diligence file and tagged trial cohort
workflow.gate: no volume commitment is signed before a trial cohort has been worked, and no vendor proceeds without producing consent artifacts

workflow.action: Define the qualification gates and script the walk-away
workflow.description: Order ownership and tenure, consumption, site red flags and financing readiness with pass, fail and not-yet outcomes, and script the plain-language disqualification for each fail reason
workflow.artifact: gate script with outcomes and disqualification language per reason
workflow.gate: every gate has a defined outcome set and every fail reason has a scripted conversation and a recorded code

workflow.action: Close the economic chain on a completed cohort
workflow.description: Compute contact, sit, close and post-signature survival for each tagged cohort and derive cost per installed and paid deal against net per project
workflow.artifact: per-channel cost-per-installed-deal sheet with cohort period, size and cash-timing
workflow.gate: every ratio comes from the operator's own records and the cash-out to cash-in lag is stated alongside the cost

workflow.action: Size the forward pipeline and fold in measured attrition
workflow.description: Work backwards from an installed-deal target through survival ratios and stage lags to the leads and held appointments required now, applying cancellation rates measured by cause and channel
workflow.artifact: dated build-ahead plan with the ratios, lags and attrition assumptions used
workflow.gate: the plan names a future month, states its required current input, and is recomputed whenever a ratio or lag moves materially

priority_rationale: The conduct identity and the position choice come first because they decide which channels, compensation mechanisms, and obligation classes are even available; the licensing, door and consent layers follow immediately because an unlawful pipeline has negative value however well it converts; compensation literacy and the clawback map precede all lead spending because they set the net per project that any acquisition cost must be justified against; the channel portfolio, vendor diligence and record layer are built before money is spent so that every later ratio is attributable; the qualification gates and the scripted walk-away sit between acquisition and pipeline because they are where the conduct rules become an observable process; and the stage model, pipeline mathematics and cancellation modelling come last because they compose everything upstream into a forward plan that uses expected rather than signed value.

dominance_rules.rule: Anti-pressure, verified-numbers conduct dominates every revenue, quota, and cash-flow consideration in this knowledge base
dominance_rules.rationale: the vertical's reputation is its only compounding asset and a single pressured or misleading sale damages it further while producing a remorse cancellation anyway
dominance_rules.trigger: any moment where closing faster or claiming more would improve a number
dominance_rules.action: hold the conduct rule, change the pipeline or the forecast instead, and record the decision

dominance_rules.rationale: the households most easily persuaded are the ones a long financial commitment can hurt most, and their consent does not make the harm acceptable
dominance_rules.trigger: any recognition signal for age, comprehension, language, fixed income, or third-party pressure
dominance_rules.action: decline a same-visit signature, involve a trusted person, run the teach-back check, and disqualify where the obligation plainly does not fit

dominance_rules.rule: Consumer-protection and contact-consent obligations dominate channel economics
dominance_rules.rationale: a channel that cannot evidence lawful contact and lawful solicitation is a liability whose expected cost is unbounded regardless of its measured conversion
dominance_rules.trigger: a channel, vendor, or territory whose consent basis or permit position is unverified
dominance_rules.action: suspend the channel until the basis is evidenced; no price or volume advantage overrides this

dominance_rules.rule: A failed screen dominates sunk acquisition cost
dominance_rules.rationale: money already spent cannot be recovered by selling to a household that should not buy, and the attempt converts a small loss into a cancellation, a complaint, or both
dominance_rules.trigger: a gate fails on a household acquired through paid or heavily worked supply
dominance_rules.action: end the conversation on the screen result, record the reason, and correct the channel that produced the misfit

dominance_rules.rule: The signed agreement dominates any recruiting claim, verbal assurance, or peer report about compensation
dominance_rules.rationale: compensation is a contractual formula and every planning figure derived from anything else describes a business that does not exist
dominance_rules.trigger: a conflict between a stated rate or promise and the agreement's own terms
dominance_rules.action: plan from the agreement and the reconciled statement, and raise the discrepancy in writing before continuing

dominance_rules.rule: The operator's own measured ratios dominate vendor-supplied and industry conversion claims
dominance_rules.rationale: conversion depends on the operator's process, market and screening standard, so imported figures are not evidence about this business
dominance_rules.trigger: any model input that would otherwise be filled from a benchmark or a vendor claim
dominance_rules.action: leave the input explicitly unmeasured and decide under stated uncertainty rather than importing a number

dominance_rules.rule: Cost per installed and paid deal dominates cost per lead in every channel decision
dominance_rules.rationale: channels differ most in what happens after the signature, which is exactly what cost per lead cannot see
dominance_rules.trigger: a channel comparison, a budget reallocation, or a vendor renewal
dominance_rules.action: decide on cancellation-adjusted installed-deal cost, and state the uncertainty where a cohort has not yet completed

dominance_rules.rule: Money inside a clawback window is not spendable income
dominance_rules.rationale: reversible advances funding fixed costs is the most common way a commission-only operator becomes insolvent while nominally profitable
dominance_rules.trigger: any spending decision drawing on funds that have not passed their final trigger
dominance_rules.action: hold the balance separately and release it only at trigger expiry

dominance_rules.rule: The installer's licensing, engineering and build responsibilities dominate any assurance the seller might give
dominance_rules.rationale: the seller is not licensed for the build and cannot deliver what belongs to the installer, the authority having jurisdiction, or the utility
dominance_rules.trigger: a homeowner asks for a commitment on production, timeline, code, structural, or electrical outcomes
dominance_rules.action: route the question to the responsible party and state plainly what the seller is and is not responsible for

dominance_rules.rule: Verified jurisdiction obligations dominate expansion speed
dominance_rules.rationale: an unlawfully generated pipeline is worth less than nothing once it produces a complaint, an enforcement action, or an unenforceable contract
dominance_rules.trigger: demand, a crew, or a partner making a new territory attractive before its register is complete
dominance_rules.action: keep the territory closed until the obligation register is complete and dated

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide the market position before signing any lead-vendor contract or engaging anyone to sell
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building a lead operation and a team around a position the operator then has to unwind, with the customer records staying behind

anti_rework_rules.rule: Reconstruct the compensation arithmetic and the clawback trigger list before forecasting income or committing lead spend
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an acquisition budget sized against a net per project that the agreement never supported, discovered only after the spend is committed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify a territory's registration, permit and contact obligations before the first knock, call, or campaign there
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a pipeline generated unlawfully that must be discarded, plus the complaint and enforcement exposure it carries

anti_rework_rules.rule: Stand up per-source tagging and stage timestamps before buying the first lead
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an entire early period of spend that can never be attributed to a channel and therefore can never inform a decision

anti_rework_rules.rule: Capture and store the consent artifact at lead intake rather than when a dispute arises
anti_rework_rules.prevents: having to reconstruct a contact basis retrospectively from a vendor who no longer has it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Establish ownership, signing authority and tenure intent before any appointment is booked or any usage data is requested
anti_rework_rules.prevents: evenings spent presenting to someone who cannot sign, and design work commissioned for a household that cannot proceed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Obtain twelve months of the homeowner's own usage before any proposal work is commissioned
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a proposal built on a peak or trough month that the seller must later contradict in front of the homeowner

anti_rework_rules.rule: Name roof, panel and approval red flags at first contact rather than leaving them to the site survey
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a project re-priced or cancelled after signature, with a homeowner who feels the cost was concealed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Route financing prequalification through the lender's own path before design or engineering effort is spent
anti_rework_rules.prevents: designed projects that fail at financing verification and reverse a milestone advance already received

anti_rework_rules.rule: Compare or scale channels only after at least one tagged cohort has completed the cycle to final payment
anti_rework_rules.prevents: scaling a channel that signs easily and cancels heavily, and retiring one that was slower but survived

iteration_protocol.trigger: contact rate on a source collapses against its own trial baseline
iteration_protocol.action: audit lead age, resale history, sharing and consent provenance with the vendor before changing scripts, representatives, or territory

iteration_protocol.trigger: cancellation rises or its cause mix shifts toward remorse
iteration_protocol.action: break the population down by cause, channel and representative, and tighten conduct and qualification before adding any lead volume

iteration_protocol.trigger: a compensation, redline, or lead-split amendment is announced
iteration_protocol.action: recompute the one-project arithmetic and the allowable acquisition cost, confirm in writing which terms govern already-signed projects, and pause discretionary spend until both are settled

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new municipality, state, or introducer class enters the plan
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the obligation verification for registration, canvass permits, contact rules and referral compensation before any activity there

iteration_protocol.trigger: a complaint, review, or family objection alleges pressure, misleading savings, or a rushed signature
iteration_protocol.action: pull the full deal record, review the conduct against the standard, retrain or remove the person involved, and re-audit live materials and scripts

iteration_protocol.trigger: the forecast of installed deals for a future month falls below target
iteration_protocol.action: recompute the build-ahead requirement and raise steady lead input now for that month, explicitly rather than tightening behaviour at the close in the current one

iteration_protocol.trigger: the installer partner's backlog or the permitting and interconnection timeline lengthens materially
iteration_protocol.action: re-model stage lags and cancellation exposure, correct the timeline language used at the point of sale, and reset income expectations and reserve size

iteration_protocol.trigger: a scheduled periodic review, or a cohort completing the cycle to final payment
iteration_protocol.action: recompute cancellation-adjusted cost per installed deal for every channel, rebalance the mix, and retire the weakest channel rather than adding a new one on top
